claims.text: GHK is an endogenous human plasma tripeptide first described in 1973; GHK-Cu is its copper complex.

Proposed mechanism: GHK-Cu modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and activates wound-healing and antioxidant gene-expression programmes — a mechanistic claim resting on reviews by the peptide's originator.
claims.reviewNote: teach as mechanism with the conflict of interest visible

claims.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small-trial: one PubMed-indexed randomized trial (post-laser wound healing, 2006) and manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic trials that are not indexed; the guides rate the cosmetic indication GRADE C.
claims.reviewNote: grade C per both guides; Omar to confirm

claims.text: Injectable GHK-Cu has no randomized human trials; use rests on anecdote, and injection-site pain and rash are common.
claims.reviewNote: safety statement is the guides' clinical observation; Li 2016 is mechanistic support only

claims.text: Whether topical GHK-Cu reaches the dermis in meaningful amounts is unsettled; penetration data are in vitro and measurement-dependent.

US status (as of May 14, 2026): GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes sits in FDA's 503A Category 1 (under evaluation) after its nomination was withdrawn on April 22, 2026 and partially reinstated; FDA intends to consult the PCAC on it before the end of February 2027. Category 1 is an enforcement posture, not approval; the injectable route has no such standing.
claims.reviewNote: more precise than either guide's 'Category 1 (non-injectable)'; date-stamp it in the lesson

claims.text: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) improved photoaging measures in a 12-week randomized trial funded by the manufacturer; the Matrixyl 3000 blend rests on the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade D; note sponsorship explicitly

claims.text: Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3/-8) mimics the N-terminus of SNAP-25; randomized placebo-controlled trials report modest wrinkle improvement, but delivery to the neuromuscular junction at cosmetic concentrations is considered implausible — the effect, if real, is not a botulinum substitute.
claims.reviewNote: PPG-Aug marks 'Wang Y et al.' as not indexed — the 2013 Am J Clin Dermatol RCT is indexed (PMID 23417317); report to the author

claims.text: Leuphasyl (pentapeptide-18) evidence consists of manufacturer studies only; no indexed human trial was found.
claims.reviewNote: no primary source exists — teach as 'no independent evidence', not as a mechanism

claims.text: Cosmetic peptides are regulated as cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is evaluated by a cosmetics framework rather than a drug-approval pathway.
claims.reviewNote: US framing; UK/EU cosmetics regulation to be added for the SEASON edition

claims.text: BPC-157 evidence is an extensive rodent literature, largely from one research group; human data are uncontrolled case series; the first randomized human trials were registered in 2026 and have no results.
claims.reviewNote: guides rate C (A&RE) — Omar to confirm; two independent 2025–26 reviews now exist

claims.text: TB-500 is the acetylated 17–23 fragment of thymosin β4 (Ac-LKKTETQ), not thymosin β4 itself; the fragment was characterized by analysing the product, and human trial data for the fragment do not exist.
KPV, the C-terminal tripeptide of α-MSH, reduces inflammation in murine colitis models; no randomized human trials exist for any indication.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade C; the 'small open-label atopic dermatitis studies' the guide mentions could not be located on PubMed

claims.text: Topical LL-37 has two randomized placebo-controlled trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers: a small first-in-human dose-ranging trial (n=34) that was positive at low dose, and a larger phase IIb trial that was negative in its full cohort — a worked example of why a small positive trial is not confirmation.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade C; both trials authored by the developer

claims.text: BPC-157, KPV and TB-500 (with MOTS-c, emideltide, semax and epitalon) were reviewed by FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee on July 23–24, 2026 for possible addition to the 503A bulks list; the committee's votes are advisory, FDA rulemaking is still required, and compounding these substances without bulks-list standing has drawn FDA warning letters.
claims.reviewNote: vote counts come from trade press, not FDA — cite them as unofficial or omit

claims.text: Research-use-only peptide products are made outside GMP and carry documented risks of impurity, inaccurate dosing and heavy-metal contamination.
claims.reviewNote: A&RE asserts heavy-metal (arsenic, lead) contamination without a citation; no primary analytical study of skin-peptide RUO products was found. Adjacent evidence only. Either the author supplies the source or the lesson says 'reported, not documented'.

claims.text: GLOW (GHK-Cu + BPC-157 + TB-500) and KLOW (+ KPV) are marketing names for research-use-only blends with no controlled human trials.
claims.reviewNote: absence-of-evidence claim; the guides are sufficient
